bearing.guide.linear_chassis_group.text_: Touching Linear Chassis of the same type lock together into one group
Push any member and the rest of the group comes with it
Chassis of a different type, or turned to another axis, don't join and are left in place
Gluing Blocks to a Linear Chassis
A Slime Ball makes either free end of a Linear Chassis sticky
Applied to an end that is already sticky, it treats the far end too
Empty-handed, Sneak + Right-Click a sticky end to clean it
Sticky ends pick up the line of blocks ahead of them; non-sticky ends do not
With a Wrench in hand, scroll over the chassis to fine-tune its reach
Keep CTRL down as you scroll to retune the reach of the whole linked group
Anything on the remaining faces has to be joined up with Super Glue
Mix these methods and builds of almost any shape will travel as a single Contraption
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.header: Gluing Blocks to a Radial Chassis
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_1: Radial Chassis of one type connect when lined up end to end
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_2: Rotate a single one and the whole column rotates
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_3: Any of its four side faces may be made sticky with slime
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_4: Applying slime to a face that is already sticky covers every other side
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_5: With nothing in hand, Sneak + Right-Click a face to wipe it clean
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_6: If some block touches one of the sticky faces...
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_7: ...all blocks connected to it in that layer, up to the radius, join in too
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_8: Use a Wrench and scroll on the chassis to fine-tune the radius
bearing.guide.radial_chassis.text_9: Anything outside the reach of the sticky faces stays behind
bearing.guide.super_glue.text_1: Super Glue groups loose blocks so a contraption carries them together
bearing.guide.super_glue.text_2: Right-Click one corner, then the opposite one, to glue the whole box between
bearing.guide.super_glue.text_3: Punch a glued box with the glue in hand to undo it
bearing.guide.super_glue.text_4: Neighbours within one glued area drag each other with them
bearing.guide.super_glue.text_5: Overlapping glued areas merge, and everything in them moves as one
bearing.guide.super_glue.text_6: Blocks that hang from or rest on something, such as this torch, usually come along anyway
bearing.guide.sticker.text_1: Stickers grab and release blocks on command from redstone
bearing.guide.sticker.text_2: Each incoming signal toggles it between gripping and letting go
bearing.guide.sticker.text_3: Carried by a contraption in this state, the block goes with it
bearing.guide.sticker.text_4: Toggle it once more and the block is dropped off where it is
bearing.guide.mechanical_piston.header: Pushing Builds with a Mechanical Piston
bearing.guide.mechanical_piston.text_1: Whatever sits ahead of a Mechanical Piston gets shoved forward
bearing.guide.mechanical_piston.text_2: Speed and direction follow the input rotation; a regular piston leaves blocks behind as it pulls back
bearing.guide.mechanical_piston.text_3: The Sticky variant drags the blocks touching its head back as well
bearing.guide.piston_pole.text_1: Without Extension Poles behind it, a Mechanical Piston can't extend at all
bearing.guide.piston_pole.text_2: Its maximum reach equals the number of poles lined up at its back
bearing.guide.mechanical_piston_modes.te: When the piston stops, the moved build turns back into normal blocks
Use the value panel to keep it as a moving entity indefinitely, or to settle only at its starting position
bearing.guide.rope_pulley.header: Lifting Builds with a Rope Pulley
bearing.guide.rope_pulley.text_1: Driven by Rotational Force, a Rope Pulley hauls the blocks under it up or down
bearing.guide.rope_pulley.text_2: Input rotation sets both its heading and its pace
bearing.guide.rope_pulley_modes.text_1: Once the pulley halts, the lowered build becomes regular blocks again
bearing.guide.rope_pulley_modes.text_2: The value panel can make it never settle, or settle only back at its starting height
bearing.guide.rope_pulley_multi_rope.tex: Once one pulley assembles the blocks beneath it...
...additional pulleys at that height latch on to the same build
The extra pulleys need no power; their ropes are decoration only
bearing.guide.rope_pulley_attachment.tex: If another contraption carries the pulley around...
...the load hanging below travels with it
Note: only an idle pulley can be carried like this
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_1: An Elevator Pulley shuttles a build vertically between floors you define
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_2: Start by building the car that should travel
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_3: Next, set up a pair of Redstone Contacts pointing at one another...
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_4: ...and glue the one on the inside onto the car
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_5: Contraption Controls let riders choose a floor from inside the car
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_6: Hook the pulley up to a rotation source
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_7: Now Right-Click the pulley: the car becomes a contraption
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_8: The contact left in place is now an Elevator Contact
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_9: Each Elevator Contact marks a floor and has settings you can edit
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_10: Any further Redstone Contacts in that column get converted too
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_11: Send a redstone pulse to a contact to call the car to that floor
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_12: The car travels as fast as the pulley spins
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_13: From inside, scroll over the controls to choose a floor and click to travel
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_14: Another Right-Click on the pulley returns the car to block form
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_15: Sliding doors fitted to the car open and shut by themselves
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_16: An Elevator Contact outputs redstone power while the car is stopped at it
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_17: Use this to open doors or trigger effects on arrival
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley.text_18: Attach a Display Link to any contact to show the car's current floor
bearing.guide.elevator_pulley_multi_rope: When one pulley puts its car together...
...other pulleys at that height connect to the same build
They can stay unpowered; the extra ropes are just for looks
bearing.guide.windmill_source.header: Windmill Bearings as a Power Source
bearing.guide.windmill_source.text_1: Whatever block is right in front of a Windmill Bearing gets grabbed
bearing.guide.windmill_source.text_2: Glue the surrounding blocks to it with Super Glue to form a single movable build
bearing.guide.windmill_source.text_3: If it contains enough sail-type blocks, the build can act as a windmill
bearing.guide.windmill_source.text_4: Right-Click the bearing to start it; it then outputs Rotational Force
bearing.guide.windmill_source.text_5: Rotation speed rises with the number of sail blocks
bearing.guide.windmill_source.text_6: Choose the spin direction on its value panel
bearing.guide.windmill_source.text_7: Right-Click again whenever you like to halt it and edit the build
bearing.guide.windmill_structure.text_1: Any build works as a windmill so long as it has 8 or more sail-type blocks, wool for example
bearing.guide.sail.text_2: They connect to neighbouring blocks and to each other automatically, with no glue or chassis
bearing.guide.sail.text_3: Use any Dye on them to recolour them
bearing.guide.sail.text_4: Shearing them reduces them to bare frames again
bearing.guide.sail_frame.text_1: Sail Frames make windmill building simple
bearing.guide.sail_frame.text_2: They connect to neighbouring blocks and to each other automatically, with no glue or chassis
bearing.guide.mechanical_bearing.header: Rotating Builds with a Mechanical Bearing
bearing.guide.mechanical_bearing.text_1: The block right in front of a Mechanical Bearing is the one it grabs
bearing.guide.mechanical_bearing.text_2: Supplied with Rotational Force, it assembles that block and all attached ones into a spinning contraption
bearing.guide.bearing_modes.text_1: On stopping, the bearing settles the build at whichever block-aligned angle lies closest
bearing.guide.bearing_modes.text_2: The value panel can stop it from ever settling, or have it settle only near its starting angle
bearing.guide.stabilized_bearings.text_1: Mount a Mechanical Bearing on a build that is moving...
bearing.guide.stabilized_bearings.text_2: ...and it will try to keep pointing upright
bearing.guide.stabilized_bearings.text_3: As usual, it picks up the block directly ahead
bearing.guide.stabilized_bearings.text_4: So the attached sub-contraption remains level throughout the ride
bearing.guide.clockwork_bearing.header: Clock Hands with a Clockwork Bearing
bearing.guide.clockwork_bearing.text_1: Clockwork Bearings take hold of what sits ahead of them
bearing.guide.clockwork_bearing.text_2: Powered by Rotational Force, it rotates the build to show the in-game hour
bearing.guide.clockwork_bearing.text_5: Right-Click it to start or stop the animation
bearing.guide.clockwork_bearing.text_6: You can add another build in front of the hour hand
bearing.guide.clockwork_bearing.text_7: Keep the two builds unglued from one another
bearing.guide.clockwork_bearing.text_8: That outer build now acts as the minute hand
bearing.guide.gantry_shaft.text_1: A Gantry Shaft is the track that carriages mounted on it slide along
bearing.guide.gantry_shaft.text_2: Blocks fixed to the carriage are carried by the gantry
bearing.guide.gantry_carriage.text_1: A Gantry Carriage mounts on a Gantry Shaft and travels along it
bearing.guide.gantry_carriage.text_2: Anything attached to the carriage travels with it
bearing.guide.gantry_redstone.text_1: A Gantry Shaft that gets a redstone signal no longer drives its carriages
bearing.guide.gantry_redstone.text_2: Its rotation is sent out through the carriage's output shaft instead
bearing.guide.gantry_direction.text_1: Gantry Shafts may point toward either end of their axis
bearing.guide.gantry_direction.text_2: A carriage's direction of travel follows the way its shaft points...
bearing.guide.gantry_direction.text_4: The rotation passed on to the output follows those same rules
bearing.guide.gantry_cascaded.text_1: Shafts join onto carriages with no Super Glue required
bearing.guide.gantry_cascaded.text_2: Carriages on a shaft that is itself moving join in the same way
bearing.guide.gantry_cascaded.text_3: Stacking gantries like this gives one system motion on multiple axes
bearing.guide.cart_assembler.text_1: A powered Cart Assembler mounts the build sitting on it onto a Minecart rolling past
bearing.guide.cart_assembler.text_2: Unpowered, it does the reverse and turns passing cart contraptions back into blocks
bearing.guide.cart_assembler.text_3: Wrench a Minecart to pack up the whole contraption and carry it away
bearing.guide.cart_assembler_modes.text_: A cart contraption swings round to point the way its cart is rolling
The assembler's arrow marks the side treated as the build's front
Switch the assembler to 'Lock rotation' to keep the build facing one way throughout
bearing.guide.cart_assembler_dual.text_1: If one build spans a pair of Cart Assemblers...
bearing.guide.cart_assembler_dual.text_2: ...a signal to either one creates a Carriage Contraption
bearing.guide.cart_assembler_dual.text_3: The two carts then travel as though linked by a Minecart Coupling
bearing.guide.cart_assembler_rails.text_: Over regular rail, a Cart Assembler leaves the motion of passing carts alone
Over Powered Rail, it keeps the cart stopped until a signal arrives
Over Controller Rail it acts alike: the cart is held until powered
A Chest Minecart works as the carrier just as well
bearing.guide.mechanical_harvester.text_: Mechanical Harvesters mounted on a moving build...
...cut every fully grown crop along the way and plant it again
bearing.guide.mechanical_plough.text_1: Mechanical Ploughs mounted on a moving build...
bearing.guide.mechanical_plough.text_2: ...smash anything in the way that lacks a solid collision box
bearing.guide.mechanical_plough.text_3: They can also till the soil beneath into farmland
bearing.guide.mechanical_plough.text_4: ...and push mobs and other entities aside, harmlessly
bearing.guide.contraption_controls.text_: Out of the box, every actor on a moving build is running
Contraption Controls turn them on or off mid-journey
Mount them anywhere on the build; position does not matter
Before assembly, set the filter to limit it to a single kind of actor
If redstone powers it at the moment of assembly...
...its actors begin in the off state
bearing.guide.mechanical_roller_pave.tex: Mechanical Rollers smooth out the terrain beside tracks and roads
Without a material, the default mode only breaks blocks in the way, drill-style
Before assembly, you can assign a paving material to it
It takes that material from chests or barrels on the same build
Now it lays fresh blocks underneath, besides clearing obstacles
Note: blocks broken by a roller might yield no drops
Trains are a natural fit, but rollers run on most other moving builds as well
bearing.guide.mechanical_roller_fill.tex: Before assembly, the roller's mode can be changed
Fill modes bridge the space between an elevated route and the terrain
'Fill Straight Down' drops simple pillars all the way to the ground
'Fill Down in a Slope' makes every lower layer slightly wider than the last
Neither fill mode removes existing blocks, unlike 'Clear Path and Pave'
bearing.guide.redstone_contact.text_1: Face two Redstone Contacts at each other and both emit a signal
bearing.guide.redstone_contact.text_2: This holds even if one of them rides on a moving build
